_comment: A routed squadron caught on its flank by spearmen gets clear of them (#1913, re-judged for #1949). A brittle player squadron (20 Cavalry at morale 0.4) stands facing west; an enemy Spearmen block (48 men, 12 files) 240 wu to its south, facing it, marches up onto its left flank with no player input. The squadron is in contact from about tick 637 and routs at tick 676 still in contact (the setup checks: IDLE at 674, ROUTING and in contact at 676). Each routed man then runs on his own from the spearmen he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), and the spearmen follow in their ranks at the edge of their reach. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch: the squadron is still in the spearmen's reach at tick 760 and out of it at tick 800 on every seed (pinned), its men's centroid running north from (899.98, 691.09) at the rout to (899.05 to 899.18, 637.7) at tick 800 on seeds 0 to 3 and from (906.3, 692.85) to (942.62, 648.07) on seed 4. #1913 pinned the squadron's couple() anchor at ticks 705, 708, 732 and 735 ((917.74, 686.78) to (920.96, 678.28), tol 5.9 wu) to guard against that anchor switching back and forth between the front ranks and the whole block at the edge of the spearmen's reach. The bottom-up flight (#1949) removed the anchor: a routed unit's position is the centroid of its men. So those four pins are retired, and the contact pin, which fails for a rout that stays in the spearmen's reach, carries the clip's claim. The squadron is still routing when the clip ends at tick 800.
